taskVersion.name: ves-real-item

parts.text:
You are preparing a groundwater site note for a borehole drilling team.

Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station Egwi, Etche LGA survey stations. Interpreted layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 295.88 | 0.54518 | 0.54518
2 | 798.6 | 3.5924 | 4.1376
3 | 864.62 | 2.1559 | 6.2935
4 | 1810.2 | 37.957 | 37.25
5 | 5634.2 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this station's curve as HAA-type.

Write a short site report (under 150 words) for station Egwi, covering the layer sequence and the curve type. End with one JSON line exactly like this:
{"curve_type_stated": "<letters>", "label_issue_flagged": true or false}
Set label_issue_flagged to true only if your report says the curve-type classification on file does not fit the layer values.

**Site Report – Station Egwi, Etche LGA**

The VES interpretation at Station Egwi reveals a five-layer subsurface sequence with resistivities increasing monotonically with depth: Layer 1 (295.88 Ω·m, 0.545 m), Layer 2 (798.6 Ω·m, to 4.14 m depth), Layer 3 (864.62 Ω·m, to 6.29 m depth), Layer 4 (1810.2 Ω·m, to 37.25 m depth), and Layer 5 (5634.2 Ω·m, infinite half-space). This suggests a progressive increase in subsurface competency/resistivity, possibly reflecting a transition from weathered/lateritic topsoil to more resistive consolidated or sandy formations at depth.

Applying the standard curve-type convention: each three-layer resistivity triplet (r1<r2<r3) yields an "A" code, giving AAA across the full sequence, which simplifies to a single-letter "A"-type curve — not HAA as recorded on file. The on-file label does not match the computed resistivity trend, as no decrease (H-break) occurs between any layers.

{"curve_type_stated": "A", "label_issue_flagged": true}
